marketInsightsHtml:
La charge de base allemande du 26 novembre a grimpé de 2,00 € à 221,70 €/MWh, la France de novembre a gagné 3,30 € pour atteindre un record de 210,75 €/MWh (dépassant janvier pour la première fois), et la Grande-Bretagne de novembre a légèrement augmenté de 0,50 £ à 191,00 £/MWh, élargissant sa prime par rapport à décembre à 7,45 £/MWh.

En France, les faibles niveaux d'eau du Rhône ont incité EDF à alerter dès dimanche sur d'éventuelles restrictions de production de la centrale nucléaire de Saint-Alban, compensant le recouplage prévu du réacteur Cattenom 4 de 1,3 GW.

marketInsights.gas:
European natural gas rebounded strongly this morning, Dutch TTF November 26 settled down €0.88 on Tuesday at €95.83/MWh, with Day-Ahead at €97.20/MWh. In the UK, NBP front-month shed 1.75p on Tuesday to settle at 236.70p/th, while Day-Ahead ticked up 0.25p to 237.55p/th. However, this morning trading saw UK prompt and front-month gas surge to near four-year highs of 243.55p/th.

The market pivoted sharply bullish overnight following reports that the US has urged several Persian Gulf nations to prepare for a potential renewed military campaign against Iran immediately following the US midterm elections. This dashed earlier optimism from Monday’s regional talks in Tehran, while exit polls from Israel's parliamentary elections show Prime Minister Netanyahu in a dead heat with Gadi Eisenkot, extending regional uncertainty. Physical LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain severely crippled, reinforced by QatarEnergy officially extending its force majeure on Edison’s 6.4 bcm/yr contract through to 30 December, bringing total missing cargoes to 38. In response to growing structural import exposure, the Dutch government formally updated its National Gas Crisis Plan, while the BBL interconnector confirmed a physical flow reversal towards Great Britain starting 29 October.

Upstream pipeline deliverability remains tight as unplanned Norwegian outages across Karstø, Oseberg, Kollsnes, and Sleipner knocked roughly 37–50 mcm/d offline on Tuesday. Total EU storage inventories stand at 74.93% capacity (848.8 TWh), the lowest seasonal level on record dating back to 2009, with Germany at 61.65%, the Netherlands at 65.53%, and the UK at 41.31%. While near-term temperatures see a final mild bump today, an expansive Scandinavian/Ural blocking high takes hold from Thursday, introducing sub-normal temperatures, morning fog, and a sharp increase in space-heating demand across Central and Western Europe.
marketInsights.power:
European power curves diverged on Tuesday as front-month contracts resisted wider gas losses, while prompt cash surged aggressively higher in anticipation of an imminent renewable collapse.

German November 26 baseload climbed €2.00 to €221.70/MWh, French November gained €3.30 to reach a record €210.75/MWh (overtaking January for the first time), and UK November edged up £0.50 to £191.00/MWh, widening its premium over December to £7.45/MWh.

Renewable generation is set to crater across the continent over the coming days. While residual Atlantic winds supported early-week output, an advancing high-pressure system will suppress wind load factors to just 3–6% between Thursday and Saturday. German wind is forecast to plunge below 3 GW, UK metered wind will average below 5 GW through 6 November, and the Netherlands drops to 2.9 GW. Combined with light winds, high dew points, and low solar irradiation, the resulting Dunkelflaute pattern is significantly raising prompt grid-balancing stress.

Generation margins face compounded operational pressures. In France, low water levels on the Rhône river prompted EDF to warn of potential generation restrictions at the Saint-Alban nuclear plant starting Sunday, offsetting the scheduled recoupling of the 1.3 GW Cattenom 4 reactor. In Germany, EnBW announced coal supply disruptions at its Altbach/Deizisau 2 unit due to logistical constraints, while commercial feed-in at the 960 MW He Dreiht and 225 MW NC 2B offshore wind farms was delayed to November.

Generation economics continue to heavily favour coal over gas, with German November 40% coal dark spreads holding near €99.45/MWh against clean sparks of €12.42/MWh, ensuring thermal units remain dispatched ahead of CCGTs to cover the renewable shortfall.
